{{Short description|Geometric surface}}
[[Image:Mathematica dinis surface.png|thumb|350px|Dini's surface plotted with adjustable parameters by [[Wolfram Mathematica]] program]]
[[File:Dini Surface.png|thumb|350px|Dini's Surface with constants a = 1, b = 0.5 and 0 ≤ u ≤ 4{{pi}} and 0<v<1.]]
In [[geometry]], '''Dini's surface''' is a [[surface (mathematics)|surface]] with constant negative [[curvature]] that can be created by twisting a [[pseudosphere]].<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://mathworld.wolfram.com/DinisSurface.html
| title = Wolfram Mathworld: Dini's Surface
| accessdate = 2009-11-12}}</ref> It is named after [[Ulisse Dini]]<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www-gap.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Dini.html
| title = Ulisse Dini Biography
| publisher = School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews, Scotland
| year = 2000
| author = J J O'Connor and E F Robertson
| accessdate = 2016-04-12
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120609144111/http://www-gap.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Dini.html
| archive-date = 2012-06-09
| url-status = dead
}}</ref> and described by the following [[parametric equation]]s:<ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://knol.google.com/k/suresh-emre/dini-s-surface-geometry/35vsnxisjn2mw/26# 
 |title=Knol: Dini's Surface (geometry) 
 |accessdate=2009-11-12 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723150222/http://knol.google.com/k/suresh-emre/dini-s-surface-geometry/35vsnxisjn2mw/26 
 |archivedate=2011-07-23 
}}</ref>
: <math>\begin{align}
x&=a \cos u \sin v \\
y&=a \sin u \sin v \\
z&=a \left(\cos v +\ln \tan \frac{v}{2} \right) + bu
\end{align}</math>
[[File:Dini's Surface.svg|thumb|350px|right|Dini's surface with 0&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''u''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;4{{pi}} and 0.01&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''v''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;1 and constants ''a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1.0 and ''b''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.2.]]
Another description is a [[generalized helicoid]] constructed from the [[tractrix]].<ref>{{cite book
| title = Bäcklund and Darboux transformations: geometry and modern applications in Soliton Theory
| url = https://archive.org/details/backlunddarbouxt00schi
| url-access = limited
| last = Rogers and Schief
| publisher = Cambridge University Press
| pages= [https://archive.org/details/backlunddarbouxt00schi/page/n46 35]–36
| year = 2002}}</ref>
